title.en: Natural deduction: proof trees and assumption scope

summary: Inspect why each inference is licensed and which assumptions remain open.
objective: Build a proof-tree workbench for conjunction and implication where I can construct (A ∧ B) → (B ∧ A) and inspect assumption discharge.
intent_signals: Build a proof-tree workbench for conjunction and implication where I can construct (A ∧ B) → (B ∧ A) and inspect assumption discharge.
example_prompts: Build a proof-tree workbench for conjunction and implication where I can construct (A ∧ B) → (B ∧ A) and inspect assumption discharge.
negative_signals: No quantifiers, disjunction, negation, classical contradiction rule or general theorem search.
not_for: No quantifiers, disjunction, negation, classical contradiction rule or general theorem search.

entities.name: Proof nodes
entities.guidance: Place premises above their conclusion with explicit rule bars. Offer nested scope frames as separable inspection layers; Z means scope-layout separation only, never strength or truth.

entities.name: Dependency inspector
entities.guidance: Click a discharged occurrence to reveal its owning introduction rule; pin all remaining assumptions beside the selected conclusion.

state_contract.model: Finite formula AST: atoms, conjunction and implication only. Nodes record rule, premise IDs, conclusion and open labeled assumption occurrences. Assumption introduces one occurrence; conjunction introduction unions dependencies, conjunction elimination preserves them, implication elimination unions them, and implication introduction removes only designated occurrences of its antecedent within its premise subtree.
state_contract.authority: The typed domain model owns each committed state and result. Geometry, labels and selection derive from that model; animation cannot certify a claim.
actions: Add an assumption, apply a supported introduction/elimination rule, or select occurrence IDs to discharge.
Inspect open assumptions at any node; delete a premise and invalidate dependent nodes.
Load the conjunction-swap exercise; undo and reset.

invariants: Accept a node only after checking rule arity, formula equality and referenced premise scope.
Two occurrences with equal formula text can have different discharge identity.
Expected exercise: closed conjunction-swap proof succeeds; A→B and B must not license A. A bound on search or an incomplete tree is not a disproof.
motion_guidance: Step commits one semantic action; pause freezes presentation and leaves the committed state inspectable. Reset cancels pending playback and restores the complete starting state.
Offer a static transition highlight and an equivalent readable table for reduced motion. Camera travel is presentation, not an inference or domain operation.
creative_affordances: Use shallow sculptural cards, restrained materials and selective focus to expose relationships. Prefer a flat readable layout whenever depth has no declared role.
known_limits: No quantifiers, disjunction, negation, classical contradiction rule or general theorem search.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no generated artifact, solver integration, runtime behavior or visual check has run.

physical_contract.scope: Abstract symbols and logical state; mesh contact, light and motion have no causal role in the model.

object_craft.structure: Place premises above their conclusion with explicit rule bars. Offer nested scope frames as separable inspection layers; Z means scope-layout separation only, never strength or truth.
object_craft.material: Matte surfaces and high-contrast labels; distinguish status with text and border style as well as color.

claims.statement: Natural-deduction proofs are assembled from local inference rules; conjunction introduction combines premise hypotheses, and implication introduction discharges selected antecedent assumptions. The resulting conclusion remains dependent on hypotheses not discharged.
claims.scope: Conjunction/implication fragment with explicit labeled assumption occurrences; no claim of a complete prover.
